resources.string: 1. Turn on the hotspot on one phone (no internet needed).\n2. Every other rider connects to that hotspot over Wi-Fi — one or several.\n3. Press Start on every phone. They find each other automatically and everyone hears everyone.
No Wi-Fi or hotspot network yet
Microphone unavailable. Check the permission or end any phone call.

Headset button: in music-quality mode it starts/ends talking; in call mode it mutes (open mic) or talks (push-to-talk). If your headset button does not respond, use the button above or the one in the notification.
Sync delay on this phone: %1$d ms
If one rider hears the music earlier, add delay on that phone.
The other rider is already playing music.
Your name (shown to the other rider)

For reliable use with the screen off:
• Battery: set RideTalk to “No restrictions” / allow background activity.
• If your phone has an “Autostart” or “Background apps” setting, allow RideTalk there (App settings).
• Lock RideTalk in the recent-apps screen so the system does not close it.
• Turn off “turn off hotspot automatically when idle” on the hotspot phone.
• If Wi-Fi keeps switching to mobile data, disable the phone’s Wi-Fi assistant / smart network switch.
Microphone permission is required to talk.

Play music in any app on this phone (Spotify, YouTube Music, a podcast app, your music player…) and everyone connected hears it. You hear it directly from that app. Android will ask to allow “screen recording” — only the audio is used, nothing on the screen is captured or sent. A few apps block audio sharing; they will stay silent.
Waiting… start playing in your music app.
This phone does not allow capturing app audio.
Sharing app audio needs Android 10 or newer.

Music and voices play in full stereo quality. To talk, tap the big button or your headset button: a beep tells you the mic is live, and after you stop talking it switches back to full quality by itself.
The headset mic is always available, hands-free. Bluetooth only carries the mic in “call” mode (mono 16 kHz), so music sounds like a phone call.
Stronger settings remove more wind and engine noise; at maximum your voice may sound a bit thinner.

While nobody is connected and nothing is playing, the mic and Bluetooth call link are switched off; they come back automatically when someone connects. After 30 minutes alone the intercom turns itself off.
